IOHN.|233}}</noinclude>to him, {{verse|chapter=6|verse=9}}† There is a boy here that hath fiue barley loaues, & tvvo fi{{ls}}hes: but vvhat are the{{ls}}e among {{ls}}o many? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=10}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aith, Make the men to {{ls}}it dovvne. And there vvas much gra{{ls}}{{ls}}e in the place. The men therfore {{ls}}ate dovvne, in number about fiue thou{{ls}}and. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=11}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore tooke the loaues: and vvhen he had giuen thankes, he di{{ls}}tributed to them that {{ls}}ate. in like maner al{{ls}}o of the fi{{ls}}hes as much as they vvould. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=12}}† And after they vvere filled, he {{ls}}aid to his Di{{ls}}ciples, Gather the fragments that are remaining, le{{ls}}t they be lo{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=13}}† They gathered therfore, and filled tvvelue ba{{ls}}kets vvith fragments of the fiue barley loaues, vvhich remained to them that had eaten. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=14}}† Tho{{ls}}e men therfore vvhen they had {{ls}}een vvhat a {{ls}}igne {{sc|Iesvs}} had done, {{ls}}aid, That this is the Prophet in deede that is to come into the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=15}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore vvhen he knevv that they vvould come to take him, and make him king, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 23. Mr. 6, 46.''}}* he fled againe into the mountaine him {{ls}}elf alone.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=16}}† And vvhen euen vvas come, his Di{{ls}}ciples vvent dovvne to the {{ls}}ea. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=17}}† And vvhen they vvere gone vp into the {{ls}}hippe, they came beyond the {{ls}}ea into Capharnáum. and now it vvas darke, and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas not come vnto them {{verse|chapter=6|verse=18}}† And the {{ls}}ea aro{{ls}}e, by rea{{ls}}on of a great vvinde that blevv. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=19}}† VVhen they had rovved therfore about fiue and tvventie or thirtie furlonges, they {{ls}}ee {{sc|Iesvs}} vvalking vpon the {{ls}}ea, and to dravv nigh to the {{ls}}hippe, and they feared. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=20}}† But he {{ls}}aith to them, It is I, feare not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=21}}† They vvould therfore haue taken him into the {{ls}}hippe: and forthvvith the {{ls}}hippe vvas at the land to vvhich they vvent.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=22}}† The next day, the multitude that {{ls}}toode beyond the {{ls}}ea, {{ls}}avv that there vvas no other boate there but one, and that {{sc|Iesvs}} had not entred into the boate vvith his Di{{ls}}ciples, but that his Di{{ls}}ciples only vvere departed: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=23}}† but other boates came in from Tiberias be{{ls}}ide the place vvhere they had eaten the bread, our Lord {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The{{ls}}e wordes do plainly import, that the giuing thankes was an effectual ble{{ls}}sing of the bread and working the multiplication thereof.}}∷ giuing thankes. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=24}}† VVhen therfore the multitude {{ls}}avv that {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas not there, nor his Di{{ls}}ciples, they vvent vp into the boates, & came to Capharnaum {{ls}}eeking {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=25}}† And when they had found him beyond the {{ls}}ea, they {{ls}}aid to him, Rabbi, when came{{ls}}t thou hither? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}wered them, and {{ls}}aid, Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, you {{ls}}eeke me not becau{{ls}}e you haue {{ls}}eene {{ls}}ignes, but becau{{ls}}e you did eate of the loaues, and vvere filled. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† {{sup|‖}} VVorke not the meate that<noinclude>{{rh||Gg|peri{{ls}}heth,}}</noinclude>
